text: The claimant, Nathaniel Brookes, lent the defendant, Rosalind Ferris, £12,000 in 2019. Ferris accepts receipt of the money but says it was a gift. I prefer the evidence of Brookes.
In cross-examination Mr Ogunleye accepted that he had signed the variation. Ogunleye's explanation for the delay was, in my judgment, unconvincing.
Meadows was a candid witness. I accept that Meadows did not see the letter until March, and that Garland never told her about it.
The appellant, Declan Stroud, appeals against the order in favour of Dr Imogen Vance. Counsel for Stroud submitted that Vance's report was not served in time.
It is common ground that Cooper and Short were partners in the business until 2021.

The appeal is allowed. The order of 4 March 2024 is set aside and the claim is remitted for rehearing. Case No. CL-2023-000417; costs reserved to the trial judge. The claimant's skeleton argument ran to 24 pages.
